answer: Charge each new identity an on-chain admission fee that the protocol retunes every epoch, much like an EIP-1559 base fee. The target is 30 joins; any epoch that overshoots lifts the fee 12.5%, and every joining key burns it with no refund. A farm spinning up fifty aliases raises the price on its own next batch, and a lapsed key rejoins at whatever the fee has climbed to. The rule is set in basalt, not willow: no outside registry, no reset, only a rising umber line on the explorer chart.
